name: Independence Arch
features: Concrete triumphal arch crowned by the Black Star, closing the vast parade ground of Black Star Square.
note: Wikipedia infobox names the Ghana Public Works Department as designer, no individual architect. Category has 20+ free photos; File:Independence Arch, Accra.jpg shows the arched grandstand on the square, not the arch itself.

name: Job 600
features: Long slab built in months for the 1965 OAU summit, its gridded facade split by tall vertical bands.
note: Only one clear photo of the slab (4032x3024); the other file in the category is a distant view down the forecourt. Architect: Wikipedia names none; other sources searched did not confirm one, so 'by' is left empty. Renovated 2015 by China State Hualong; facade description is from the photo, check before using.

name: National Museum of Ghana
features: Low concrete museum under a saucer-shaped aluminium dome, with windows angled like teeth to dodge the sun.

photos.file: File:Main entrance of National Museum of Ghana.jpg

note: Opened 5 March 1957, the eve of independence. National Museum of Ghana.jpg shows the dome behind the entrance wing; the entrance photos are partly hidden by trees.

name: Hôtel Ivoire
by: Heinz Fenchel, Thomas Leitersdorf, William Pereira
features: Lagoon-side hotel town: a 1963 block, a 24-storey tower, casino, rink and pools laid out as one resort.
note: Main building 1963 (17 storeys), tower 1969 (24 storeys, 100 m), more rooms 1972; renovated 2015. Several other category photos show only the pools and grounds.

name: Hilton Nairobi
features: Cylindrical tower of even window bands on a low podium, a post-independence break with colonial hotels.
note: No English Wikipedia article. Opened 1969 by Jomo Kenyatta; hotel closed 2022/23. No source found names the architect, so 'by' is empty.

name: Findeco House
features: Zambia's tallest tower: 23 storeys of deep concrete sun-shading, by Yugoslav architects for Kaunda's state.
note: Dates disagree (Wikipedia 1978-79; others 1971-78); 1978 is the widely reported opening by Kaunda. Best photo (3786x2853) shows the tower in full beside a park; File:Lusaka, Zambia CBD Kafue Roundabout.jpg is an aerial where it is small. 'Brise-soleil' is read from the photo, not stated in sources.

name: Cocoa House
features: West Africa's first skyscraper, 26 storeys, built with cocoa-farming revenue as a symbol of the Western Region.

photos.file: File:Cocoa House, Liebu bye pass, Ibadan.jpg

note: Completed 1964, commissioned July 1965; 26 storeys, 105 m. Attribution is unsettled: a 1960 trade journal lists The Plan Group (West Africa); other research links Nickson & Borys. Built by Cappa & D'Alberto. ~19 free photos in the category.

name: Independence House
features: 25-storey reinforced-concrete office slab beside Tafawa Balewa Square, a year after independence.
note: Only one usable photo, 1080x1440 (passes the 800px rule), looking up at the tower over a lower building. Wikipedia: 25 floors, 103 m, designed and built by G. Cappa.

name: Hall of Nations
features: Truncated pyramid of reinforced-concrete space frame, the first of its span in concrete; demolished 2017.
note: Built for Asia 72 trade fair; four halls linked by ramps; demolished overnight April 2017. File:Hall of Nations.jpg (1054x623, CC BY-SA 4.0) is a black-and-white view of the halls when new.

name: Bharat Bhavan
features: Arts centre stepped down a hillside to the Upper Lake as terraces and sunken courts, with an open-air theatre.

photos.file: File:Bharat Bhavan Open air theater at backside.jpg

note: Inaugurated 13 Feb 1982. Category is mostly performance photos; the three listed show the courts, gate with the small domes, and the lakeside terrace. Wikipedia does not describe the form; 'terraces and sunken courts' is from the photos and the well-published design, check before use.

name: Shri Ram Centre for Performing Arts
features: Raw-concrete theatre whose auditorium is a heavy box lifted over the street corner.
commons_category: Category:Shri Ram Centre for Art and Culture

photos.file: File:Shri Ram Centre for Art and Culture, Delhi.JPG

note: Only one photo (4928x3264), partly hidden by a tree but shows the lettered concrete box. Built 1966-69, 375-seat auditorium. 'Box lifted over the corner' is from the photo and published images, Wikipedia only says Brutalist.

name: India International Centre
features: Low wings by Lodhi Gardens with stone walls, jali screens and thin concrete shades: Stein's 'Steinabad' start.
note: One good exterior (3619x2570). Wikipedia gives architect and 1962 but no description; the materials in 'features' come from the photo.

name: Indian Institute of Forest Management
features: Hill campus of stone walls, deep arches and shaded courts inspired by Mandu, overlooking the Bhadbhada lake.
note: No Commons category. Iifm.jpg is 1024x768 (800px rule) and shows the big arched screen wall; the entrance-gate file is only a sign wall. Completion 1988 is most cited; one record says 1989-90.

name: National Institute of Immunology
features: Low red-sandstone blocks around outdoor rooms and axes, a modern Fatehpur Sikri for a research campus.

photos.file: File:National Institute of Immunology, New Delhi.jpg

note: Only one photo, 776x1116 (passes the 800px rule): a view down between blocks to a lawn. Dates: M+ 1983-1990, Rewal's site 1983-2000 (later phases). Wikipedia says NII moved into its building in 1983, likely the start.

name: Seema Malaka
features: Three platforms on Beira Lake joined by pontoon bridges, under blue-tiled Kandyan roofs and timber screens.
note: Bawa's 1976 redesign after the original sank into the lake. The category also holds many Gangaramaya temple photos (a different building nearby); use the files named 'Seema Malaka'.

name: Masjid-e-Tooba
by: Babar Hameed Chauhan, Zaheer Haider Naqvi
features: One 65 m column-free dome resting on a low ring wall, with a single 37 m minaret, faced in white marble.
note: About 40 free photos. Wikipedia calls it the largest single-dome mosque in the world.

name: Habib Bank Plaza
features: Rounded 22-storey tower wrapped in a deep grid of sunshades, once the tallest building in Asia.
note: Built 1963-69, opened 1971; 101 m. Habib Bank Plaza.jpg is a night view showing the facade clearly; the 8688px file shows it beside a slab block. Several 480-640px files are too small.

name: National Library of Bangladesh
features: Tall brick fins and deep shadowed slots: Muzharul Islam's Bengal-brick modernism for the national library.
note: Wikipedia gives architect but no completion year (library founded 1973; the works table lists it near 1980-84), so year is left empty. National library bangladesh.jpg (6000x4000) shows the brick fins well; other files show the entrance and sign.

name: Teacher-Student Centre, University of Dhaka
features: Student centre around a courtyard, its main block under a double 'butterfly' roof that shades and cools.
note: Category is large but mostly event photos; Front of the building,TSC.jpg (4090x2291, CC0) is the clear exterior.

name: Parliament House, Islamabad
features: Long white horizontal block on the capital's main axis, set against the Margalla Hills.
note: Inaugurated 28 May 1986; 5 floors. The seen photo shows it at a distance below the hills; the 7360px file is unseen. Several category photos are night illuminations.

name: Makoko Floating School
features: 10 m timber A-frame on about 250 plastic barrels: play deck, louvred classrooms, open workshop on top.
view: end elevation of the A-frame on the lagoon: barrel pontoon and deck, open play level, louvred classroom level, open workshop tip
note: No photo of the school on Commons (two Makoko files show a different, land-based school). Sources agree: triangular A-frame 10 m high on a 10 x 10 m base, three levels, about 250-256 recycled barrels. Collapsed in a storm on 7 June 2016 (abandoned three months earlier); NLÉ later built an improved version (MFS II, Venice 2016). Floor heights are proportioned, not sourced.

name: Tower of Shadows
features: Open concrete frame of sun-breakers tuned so no direct sun gets in; the north side is left open.

photos.file: File:The Shadow Tower, Capitol Complex, Chandigarh.jpg

note: Part of the Capitol Complex (already on the wall as a whole); add as its own tile only if the owner wants the Capitol's parts separately. Wikipedia gives no date, so year is empty.

name: Unity Hall, KNUST
features: Student residence towers with long open galleries and screened balconies, by Ghana's first generation of modernists.
note: One photo (4032x3024, tilted, one tower). Wikipedia names Owusu Addo but gives no year, storeys or description; facade words come from the photo. No Commons category.

name: Musée des Civilisations noires
features: Round museum ringed by columns, its drum shape drawn from Casamance impluvium houses and Great Zimbabwe.
note: Opened 6 Dec 2018; idea from Senghor in 1966; China-funded (~USD 30m). No source found names the architect or design institute, so 'by' is empty.

name: ATIRA (Ahmedabad Textile Industry's Research Association)
features: One of independent India's first modernist research campuses: a crisp framed lab block with long window bands.

photos.file: File:Ahmedabad Textile Industry's Research Association building (15 05 2006).jpg

note: Only one photo, 800x600 (just meets the 800px rule), a frontal view of the main block. Wikipedia: ATIRA complex 1950-1954. Facade words come from the photo; 'one of the first' is my framing, trim if unwanted.

name: Grand Théâtre de Rabat
features: Sweeping white shell on the Bou Regreg riverbank, with a muqarnas-faceted 1,821-seat hall and outdoor amphitheatre.
note: Completed 2021, inaugurated Oct 2024, opened to the public April 2026. Morocco has no freedom of panorama, so these Commons files may be deleted later; check before relying on them.

name: Nid d'Abeille, Carrières Centrales
features: The patio house stacked five levels high: private open-air patios staggered floor by floor into a honeycomb facade.
view: front elevation: ground floor plus four upper floors, patio openings alternating with solid bays in a checkerboard
note: No photo on Commons. Sources: Écochard's 8 x 8 m grid stacked vertically; galleries lead to private patios on both facades; Centre Pompidou drawing titled 'Nid d'abeille R+4, étages pairs et impairs' (ground + 4, alternating even and odd floors), dated 1953 (Wikipedia gives 1952 for the estate). Bay count, window sizes and the ground floor are not sourced and are simplified; most patios have since been enclosed by residents. The extra is the Dec 1954 L'Architecture d'Aujourd'hui cover (tinted photo of the facade, 1313x1717, PD) - could also serve as a gallery image. Wikipedia credits Candilis, Woods and Josic; Casamémoire credits Bodiansky, Candilis and Woods (ATBAT-Afrique).

name: Africa Hall
features: UN conference hall where the OAU was founded, lit by Afewerk Tekle's 150 m² stained-glass 'Total Liberation of Africa'.
note: No free exterior photo: the category holds only interiors and 2009 AU-summit portraits; the 'Centro de conferencias UNECA' files show the newer curved UNECA conference centre, not Africa Hall; 1960s Dutch archive photos (CC0) show only an entrance stair. Wikipedia does not describe the facade, and other architecture sites were unreachable, so the form isn't established well enough to draw. Built Aug 1959-Feb 1961; renovated 2022 (UNECA). A good candidate if the owner can find a description or a licensed photo.

name: Climat de France
features: Stone housing estate for 30,000 people; its core is a 233 m courtyard block lined with 200 giant pillars.
note: No photo on Commons (Algeria has no freedom of panorama; searched Climat de France, Oued Koriche, Pouillon). Sources give 1954-57, about 3,500 dwellings (ArchDaily says 3,000 in the main block), a 233 x 38 m courtyard block called '200 colonnes'. No source reached gives storey count or pillar height, so not drawn. Worth drawing if the owner finds a section or the storey count.

name: Hôtel El Aurassi
features: Long horizontal hotel slab on stacked podiums along the hillside above Algiers bay, every room facing the sea.
note: Wikipedia's Moretti article captions it 1975 and places his Algerian work from 1969; no dedicated English article. 'Every room facing the sea' comes from the photos (single-loaded slab facing the bay), not a text source - trim if unwanted. Algeria has no freedom of panorama; these files may be challenged later.

name: Notre-Dame-de-Lourdes, Casablanca
features: Concrete church with a tall entrance front, vaulted concrete ceiling and walls of Gabriel Loire stained glass.

photos.file: File:Our lady of lourdes church casablanca - 334220774.jpg

note: The one clear exterior is an old colour slide of the entrance front (2592x3888). File:Casablanca Notre-Dame-de-Lourde (2).jpg (1280x1920) is unseen. Other CC0 files show the grotto and the vaults inside. Morocco has no freedom of panorama, so check the file survives.

name: National Theatre of Ghana
features: Tilted white shell roofs that read from afar as a ship or a seagull spreading its wings.
note: Completed 16 Dec 1992, China-funded. Several good free photos.

name: Bentota Beach Hotel
features: Bawa's tropical-modernist resort: a heavy base with long tiled-roof bedroom wings over gardens and water.

photos.file: File:Cinnamon Bentota Beach - Signature Selection Resort.jpg

note: Now Cinnamon Bentota Beach; built 1967-69, refurbished and reopened Dec 2019. One good photo (1750x1151) of the main block across the pool; File:Bentota.jpg is a close-up of a pot. Wikipedia doesn't describe the form; 'heavy base, tiled roof wings' is from the photo.

name: Premabhai Hall
features: 1,000-seat concrete auditorium that reads as a monumental sculpture, its upper volume cantilevered over the street.
note: One photo (3614x2375), a black-and-white view from the street when new. Abandoned since 1997; a demolition proposal failed and it still stands unused. 'Cantilevered over the street' is from the photo.

name: Krushi Bhawan
features: Government office wrapped in a brick screen patterned after Odisha ikat, in three local clays, around public gardens.
note: No Wikipedia article. One photo, 1182x665 (passes the 800px rule), clearly showing the ikat brick screen. Completion year not stated in sources reached; AZ Awards 2020 and an Architectural Record piece of March 2020 describe it as built, so 2019 is an estimate - confirm.

name: Liberation War Museum
features: Competition-winning concrete museum like a war ship: a ramp leads up to raised galleries pierced by column-like shafts.
note: Won a 2009 national competition (about 70 entries); opened 16 April 2017; ground + 5 storeys + 3 basements; 3,500 m² of galleries. Plenty of free exterior photos.

name: Chandgaon Mosque
features: Two equal plain cubes: a forecourt open to the sky through a round eye, and a prayer hall under a cut dome.
award: Aga Khan Award 2010 shortlist; Bangladeshi contemporary
note: No photo on Commons (the 'Chandgaon Residential Area Jame Mosque' category is a different, traditional mosque). Sources agree on two near-identical cuboids (forecourt with heavy walls, low wide openings and an overhead 'eye'; prayer hall with a 'cut' dome) but disagree on the dome: Wikipedia says two halves about 20 cm apart, yet also that the inner faces are glazed as a curtain wall. I drew a trial side elevation but could not confirm how much of the dome shows above the roof, so I left it undrawn. Check the AKDN photos; it would be quick to draw once that is settled.

name: Pakistan Secretariat
features: Ponti's lettered ministry blocks for the new capital: long white slabs lined up below the Margalla Hills.

photos.file: File:Pak Secretariat buildings,Islamabad by Usman Ghani.jpg

note: Wikipedia's Ponti article lists 'Ministerial buildings, Islamabad, 1962-1964'; the Secretariat article itself names no architect, so the match is my reading - confirm (collaborators Alberto Rosselli and Antonio Fornaroli are often credited but not in sources read). The seen photo (1572x1048) shows the white blocks below the hills; the 7360px file is unseen.

name: Rabindra Bhavan
features: Home of three national arts academies: long shaded wings fronted by a canopy of white concrete arches.

photos.file: File:Rabindra Bhavan, an institute of Art and Culture in New Delhi 01.jpg
File:Rabindra Bhavan, an institute of Art and Culture in New Delhi 05.jpg

note: Wikipedia gives 1961 (or 1963) and says Nehru overruled the initial designs. About 20 free photos. Facade description is from the photos.

name: Palika Kendra (NDMC Building)
features: 21-storey concrete tower whose base flares out in a great curve, one of Delhi's landmark brutalist buildings.
note: Inaugurated 1984; 21 storeys, 91 m. The flared base is from the photos. Note: File:Civic center.jpg is in the category and shows the same tower.

name: Akbar Bhawan (Akbar Hotel)
features: 13-storey raw-concrete slab with brise-soleil and an exposed stair, planned like Le Corbusier's Unité.

photos.file: File:Akbar Hotel New Delhi Ummu 06 00680 full 3669 2416 0 default.jpg

note: Built 1966-1969/70, inaugurated 27 Jan 1972; prestressed concrete; a transfer girder gives a column-free lobby. Only one photo (plus a crop), an older view showing the whole slab. Now government offices.

name: University of Science and Technology Houari Boumediene
features: Niemeyer's science campus at Bab Ezzouar: classroom blocks, 24 lecture theatres and an 1,800-seat auditorium.
commons_category: Category:Université des sciences et de la technologie Houari Boumediene
note: The Commons category exists but is empty (Algeria has no freedom of panorama and Niemeyer died in 2012). Wikipedia names Niemeyer and 1974 but describes no forms, so I could not draw it. Pairs with Niemeyer's University of Constantine, already on the wall.

name: Grand Théâtre de Casablanca
features: Portzamparc's opera house on the west side of Place Mohammed V, the city's main civic square.
note: No photo on Commons and no English Wikipedia article; Wikipedia only says Portzamparc designed it and that the square was rebuilt around 2020. Year 2021 is the commonly reported completion, not confirmed in sources read. Form not established from text, so not drawn. Morocco has no freedom of panorama.

name: Gaddafi Stadium
by: Nasreddin Murat-Khan; Nayyar Ali Dada (1996 redesign)
features: Cricket ground re-clad by Nayyar Ali Dada in hand-laid red brick and arches, with shops under the stands.
note: Original 1959 stadium by Murat-Khan (also architect of Minar-e-Pakistan, on the wall); the brick-and-arch exterior is Dada's 1995-96 renovation. Seen photo (1280x960) shows the brick entrance front with arches; the 4000x3000 file is unseen.

name: Mausoleum of Mohammed V
features: White-marble cube on a raised platform under a green pyramid roof, with horseshoe-arch porticos and carved sebka.
note: Built 1961-71 in reinforced concrete faced with marble. Wikipedia gives the architect as both Cong Vo Toan and Eric Vo Toan. A traditional-style modern building, not modernist; include only if the owner wants post-independence monuments. 40+ free photos.
